data.body:
ACs AMENDED: the three WRITING-mode live criteria are RELOCATED to J9 [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36],
not dropped, by operator decision ('new story').

WHY THIS IS NOT WEAKENING THE ORACLE, which is the obvious objection:
 * The live TESTS stay in this story's deliverable — tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py
   is written, merged, collected by the jira-dc-harness CI job, and unchanged. J9's ACs require them to
   pass UNMODIFIED (an explicit 'git diff shows that file unchanged' criterion), so the oracle cannot be
   adjusted to fit the fix.
 * The requirement survives at EPIC level: J9 is a child of e369, so the epic still cannot close without
   a proven live writing pass.
 * What this story genuinely cannot do is satisfy them: a writing pass crashes on
   set_entity_property [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5], a method the CORE calls from three sites that the
   TicketTransport Protocol never declared. That is a port defect outside this story's landed scope.

WHAT THIS STORY DID PROVE LIVE, and it is not nothing: a DRY-RUN pass against a real Jira Data Center
instance completed with no unhandled exception (CI run 30604756524,
test_dc_reconcile_pass_raises_no_unhandled_exception PASSED). And the subprocess mechanism I built for
the zero-unhandled-exceptions AC is exactly what CAUGHT the set_entity_property crash — a defect the
entire unit tier, the contract suite, and 1636 reconciler tests all reported as green. The mechanism
earned its place on its first real run.

Remaining unmet ACs on this ticket: none. All non-live criteria are met and evidenced above; the live
writing criteria now live on J9.
